title: Sandbox or test-mode credential of a secret-bearing type
description: A credential of a secret-bearing type that the provider issues in a sandbox, test or non-production mode, with a mode marker in its prefix. Distinct from the provider's own publishable or public-test values.
semantics: A mode marker (test, sandbox) names the environment the credential acts in; it does not by itself change the credential's type. Where the provider documents the type as not safe to expose, the sandbox form of that type is the same kind of secret in a lower-stakes environment, and a mode word or label elsewhere in the text does not turn it into a public value. Instances whose type the provider documents as safe to expose (a publishable key) are the near-neighbor benign twins; the outcome is therefore set per case.

applicability.rationale: Stripe is the provider whose pages were read for this scenario (sandbox and live keys share one key-type table). Other providers with test or sandbox modes are added only after their own pages are read.

evidenceBasis.rationale: Stripe's API keys page lists secret and restricted keys as not safe to expose and states that sandbox keys start with sk_test_ / rk_test_ and publishable ones with pk_test_; the page gives no mode-based exemption. Reading 'a sandbox secret key is the same type' from the table is a step a reviewer can repeat; the page does not use the word 'confidential' for sandbox keys. Provider scope only; no other provider's mode behaviour is claimed.

sources.supports: Key types table: publishable keys are safe to expose, restricted and secret keys are not; sandbox keys start with pk_test_, rk_test_ and sk_test_; each mode has its own set of API keys.
sources.locator: sections 'Key types' and 'Sandbox versus live mode'
